note:
Publishes the widened Matrixyl cream banner to the Firming & Skin Density hero and makes the four section changes the new picture needs.

THE SETTINGS MATTER AS MUCH AS THE IMAGE. Three attempts and about $0.50 were spent on 2026-08-24 reworking a collection banner whose real fault was enable_parallax; the rule since is to read the section's own settings before touching the asset. Here:

  enable_parallax  set false EXPLICITLY. It was absent from this section, so it was taking the schema default, and the theme's own help text says 'Parallax crops images' — it renders at 130% and pans, so no supplied aspect ratio survives it.
  overlay_opacity  70 -> 25. Seventy is a heavy dark wash that turned the previous placeholder flat grey; 25 is what the four collection banners use.
  desktop_text     centre -> middle left. Centre puts the heading across her face, which is the exact fault just fixed on /collections/glutathione.
  mobile_image     added. One landscape image centre-cropped to a near-square on a phone loses the jar; the 1000x848 crop keeps jar and face together.

CSS is additive, in a custom-html section (.claude/rules/shopify.md 2 and 3 — no Liquid touched). It is scoped by .shopify-section--image-with-text-overlay, the section-TYPE class, not by section id: ids render as shopify-section-template--<theme id>__<key>, so an id selector built by hand silently matches nothing. This page has exactly one section of that type.

Braces are kept on separate lines deliberately: Shopify rejects an html setting containing '{{' or '}}' with a 422, and minified CSS produces ';}}' the moment a rule closes inside a media query.

settings.html:
<style>@media screen and (min-width: 700px) {
  .shopify-section--image-with-text-overlay .content-over-media > picture > img { object-position: 78% center; }
  .shopify-section--image-with-text-overlay .content-over-media > div { max-width: clamp(280px, 30vw, 480px); }
}
@media screen and (max-width: 699px) {
  .shopify-section--image-with-text-overlay .content-over-media::before {
    background-image: linear-gradient(to top,
      rgba(10, 14, 22, 0.85) 0%,
      rgba(10, 14, 22, 0.62) 22%,
      rgba(10, 14, 22, 0.00) 58%);
  }
}</style>
